title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short handwritten correction or insertion, marked '(cor)' and set off by a marginal line. It is written on the back of a typed exam sheet (Problème MP 2, on series Σ u_n c_n), so the printed text showing through is unrelated to it. The note belongs to the notes for the 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex.

There is a filtered family of abelian categories M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ … ⊂ M_N ⊂ …, presumably modules or crystals of 'level' or 'order' ≤ N in the divided-power setting. It comes with these functors:
- i_N: an inclusion-type functor between consecutive levels.
- q_N, a left-adjoint-type functor that commutes with direct limits (lim→).
- q^N, a right-adjoint-type functor that commutes with inverse limits (lim←).
- τ_N and τ̄_N: 'truncation' or graded-piece functors that commute with all limits and colimits.

The note asserts four things:
1. τ̄_N and τ_N commute with all inductive and projective limits.
2. q_N commutes with lim→ and q^N with lim←, as left and right adjoints would.
3. i_N and q^N are fully faithful, while q_N and q̄_N are localization functors.
4. When Γ (probably a divided-power functor) is exact and commutes with lim→ and lim←, τ_N is the localization of M_N by a thick (Serre) abelian subcategory stable under both kinds of limit. That subcategory is precisely M_{N-1}, so M_{N-1} gets an intrinsic description inside M_N as the kernel of τ_N.

In modern terms this is a recollement / TTF-triple picture. M_{N-1} ⊂ M_N is a bilocalizing Serre subcategory: its inclusion has both adjoints. The quotient M_N/M_{N-1} is reached by τ_N, which is exact and preserves limits and colimits. The note serves the inductive dévissage of level-N objects through their level-(N−1) part and an associated graded piece.
errors: Both i_N and q^N are called fully faithful while q_N is a localization. If i_N is a fully faithful inclusion with adjoints q_N and q^N, then the adjoints are the localizations and the inclusion is the fully faithful functor. The notation is either inconsistent or refers to different arrows (q^N possibly being a section going the other way). The deciphering of 'i_N', 'q^N', 'q̄_N' is uncertain.

The condition '(lorsque Γ est exact …)' is a hypothesis added in passing. Without it, the claim that τ_N commutes with all limits and that its kernel is exactly M_{N-1} would need proof; none is given on the page.

ideas.what: A Serre subcategory stable under both limits and colimits, whose inclusion has left and right adjoints; τ_N realizes the quotient
ideas.modern_name: Bilocalizing Serre subcategory / TTF triple / recollement of abelian categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gabriel (1962) for localization of abelian categories; Jans (1965) for TTF theories; Beilinson–Bernstein–Deligne (1982) for recollement; Franjou–Pirashvili and Kuhn for abelian recollements
ideas.where_published: Localization by thick subcategories appears in the Tôhoku-era circle and Gabriel's thesis; this specific level-N tower is unpublished as far as known

ideas.what: Level-N filtration of (divided-power) module categories, with the level-(N−1) category characterized intrinsically as the kernel of a truncation functor
ideas.modern_name: Order/level filtrations, e.g. Berthelot's arithmetic D-modules of level m, or degree filtration of polynomial functors with graded quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (1990s) for levels of divided powers; Pirashvili and others for polynomial functor recollements

deep.surprise_reason: These are formal category-theoretic remarks: adjoint functors commuting with limits, and a localization by a thick subcategory stable under limits. They are standard. The context (the precise level-N categories in the divided-power de Rham setting) is too fragmentary on this page to support a claim of new content.
transcription_corrections: '(cor)' in the upper-left corner is probably a marker for 'correction' or an insertion to be placed in the main text.
'(lorsque Γ est exact, et commute aux lim→ et lim←;)' is the most plausible reading of the parenthetical after 'Pour τ_N'.
The crossed-out word before 'Pour τ_N' is illegible.
The functor read as 'q̄_N' (written with a bar or stroke) may be 'q^N' with a correction.
